content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text makes a two-way word-count/verse ambiguity a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of single-verse openness K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand' — weighed whether a two-way word-count is allowed to support UNDERDETERMINED as open ambiguity, or whether both senses must stand and cannot ground UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"The judge treats the two-way almah/bethulah word-count as part of the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's requirement that a verse carrying two senses is not open and both senses stand."}
